question.text: Nifty is at 17,400. A call option with strike 17,500 has a premium of Rs. 85. What is its intrinsic value and time value?

answer.text: Intrinsic value: Rs. 0, Time value: Rs. 85
Intrinsic value: Rs. 85, Time value: Rs. 0
Intrinsic value: Rs. 100, Time value: Rs. -15
Intrinsic value: Rs. -100, Time value: Rs. 185

explanation.text: The Logic: Call Intrinsic Value = max(S - X, 0) = max(17,400 - 17,500, 0) = Rs. 0. The call is OTM because S < X and therefore has zero intrinsic value. Time Value = Premium - IV = 85 - 0 = Rs. 85, meaning the entire Rs. 85 premium is time value. The Trap: "IV Rs. 85, TV Rs. 0" treats the option as ITM. "IV Rs. 100, TV Rs. -15" allows a negative time value, which is impossible. "IV Rs. -100" allows negative intrinsic value, which is also impossible — IV is floored at zero. Note: Broken comparison after "This call is OTM (S" repaired — explanation now states "the call is OTM because S < X and therefore has zero intrinsic value."
